text_blocks.snippet: After a Mallory-Weiss tear, focus on soft, bland foods to allow your esophagus to heal. Avoid anything that could irritate the area, like hard or crunchy foods, spicy dishes, or acidic fruits. Good options include applesauce, yogurt, oatmeal, mashed potatoes, and soups.

list.snippet: Soft and Bland: Oatmeal, yogurt, mashed potatoes, soft-cooked vegetables, pudding, and custard.
Soups: Broth-based soups with soft ingredients like pureed vegetables.
Fruits: Soft, ripe fruits like bananas, avocados, and canned or cooked fruits without seeds.
Lean protein: Boiled or scrambled eggs, grilled chicken (if well-cooked and not dry).
Hydration: Water, herbal tea, and other clear liquids are important for hydration and healing.
Hard or Crunchy Foods: Crackers, nuts, pretzels, and raw vegetables.
Spicy Foods: Anything with chili peppers, hot sauce, or other spices.
Acidic Foods: Citrus fruits (oranges, lemons, grapefruits), tomatoes, and acidic juices.
Fibrous Foods: Celery, artichokes, and other foods with tough fibers.
Alcohol: Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can irritate the esophagus and increase the risk of further bleeding, according to Columbia University.
Medications that can increase bleeding: Avoid aspirin and NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen, according to Lybrate.
